name: SigLIP 2
plain: Google's SigLIP 2 image encoders (B, L, So400m, g): image features aligned with text, at several resolutions.
summary: SigLIP 2 (Tschannen et al. 2025, Google) image towers: ViT-B / L / So400m / g (fixed-resolution checkpoints), patch tokens + attention-pool embedding at any size; the native resolution is in the id.

papers.title: SigLIP 2: Multilingual Vision-Language Encoders with Improved Semantic Understanding, Localization, and Dense Features

official.reason: The authors' code and checkpoints are JAX (big_vision); timm's PyTorch port carries the same weights.

limitations: kernels replays a CUDA graph per small input shape without hidden states (up to about 1M activations: ViT-B ~460 px, ViT-L ~300 px), captured on the shape's second call, at most 4 per model; `model.release_graphs()` frees them.

Small kernels calls (graph-sized, with or without `layers`) run GEMMs of at most 600 tokens on cuBLAS: faster in a graph replay (ViT-B/16 224 px: 1.26 against 1.52 ms), about 10 % slower eagerly on ViT-T / B; a replay equals the eager call bit for bit.
`fp32_accumulate = true` puts every GEMM on cuBLAS with fp32 accumulation (the portable precision; slower on GeForce).
task_io: Input: one RGB image. Output: dense patch features and a pooled image feature.

parity.text: CPU, float32: max |diff| <= 0.0001 vs the original. GPU, float16 (the default), portable and kernels: mean |diff| <= 6.5 % and p99 <= 65 % of the reference's median |value| (absolute error of the output `last_hidden_state`).
